results.query: What is the first-line antibiotic, dose basis, and duration for acute otitis media in a child?
results.answer_text:
For Acute Otitis Media in a child OPD presentation:
• First-line antibiotic: Amoxicillin 40 mg/kg/day in three divided doses for 5 days.
• Severe presentation or age <6 months: Amoxicillin–Clavulanate 40 mg/kg/day (amoxicillin component).
• Pain management: Paracetamol 15 mg/kg per dose every 6 h as needed.
Citation: [STW-PED-01 v2024.1: FIRST-LINE MANAGEMENT, p.1]

results.query: What is the first-line initial drug therapy for newly diagnosed adult hypertension? (Note: the pack may contain more than one edition of this workflow.)
results.answer_text:
The STW pack contains two distinct historical editions for Hypertension Initial Management:

1. CURRENT GUIDANCE — STW-GP-02 Version 2025.2 (Effective: 2025-06-01):
• First-line initial monotherapy: Start Amlodipine 5 mg once daily OR Telmisartan 40 mg once daily.
• Uncontrolled at 4 weeks: Combine Amlodipine + Telmisartan.
• Still uncontrolled: Add Hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg.
Citation: [STW-GP-02 v2025.2: FIRST-LINE MANAGEMENT (CURRENT), p.1]

2. ARCHIVE / SUPERSEDED GUIDANCE — STW-GP-02 Version 2021.1 (Effective: 2021-02-01):
• First-line initial monotherapy: Start Atenolol 50 mg once daily as initial monotherapy.
• Stated Alternative: Hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg once daily.
• Review at 6 weeks.
• Status: Explicitly superseded by Version 2025.2.
Citation: [STW-GP-02 v2021.1: FIRST-LINE MANAGEMENT (THIS 2021 EDITION), p.1]

[NOTE ON DIVERGENCE]: Per Binding Law, both editions are presented with their respective effective dates; the system never synthesizes a third blended recommendation.

results.query: Which analgesic class must be avoided in suspected dengue, and why?
results.answer_text:
In suspected Dengue Fever in OPD management:
• AVOID: Ibuprofen, Diclofenac, Aspirin and all NSAIDs.
• Stated Reason: Bleeding risk.
• Recommended Analgesic / Antipyretic: Paracetamol 500–650 mg every 6 h for fever (maximum 3 g/day adult) with adequate oral fluids.
Citation: [STW-GP-04 v2024.2: OPD MANAGEMENT, p.1]

results.query: What are the ORS volumes after each loose stool for a child aged 2–10 years, and what zinc course accompanies it?
results.answer_text:
For Acute Gastroenteritis in Child OPD:
• ORS volume after every loose stool:
  - 100–200 ml for children aged 2–10 years
  - 50–100 ml for children aged <2 years
• Zinc supplementation course:
  - Zinc 20 mg once daily for 14 days (10 mg once daily if age <6 months)
• Feeding: Continue feeding; ondansetron 0.15 mg/kg single dose only for persistent vomiting.
• DO NOT: No routine antibiotics; no antimotility agents in children.
Citation: [STW-PED-03 v2024.1: FIRST-LINE MANAGEMENT, p.1]

results.query: Which red flags in acute low back pain mandate imaging or referral?
results.answer_text:
Red Flags in Acute Low Back Pain that mandate imaging or referral:
• Saddle anaesthesia, bladder/bowel involvement, progressive weakness
• Fever with spinal tenderness
• Significant trauma
• Age >65 with new pain + weight loss
Citation: [STW-ORT-01 v2023.1: RED FLAGS — IMAGE/REFER, p.1]

results.query: Which urinary antibiotic is avoided at 36+ weeks of pregnancy, and what is the stated alternative?
results.answer_text:
In Urinary Tract Infection in Pregnancy:
• Antibiotic avoided at 36+ weeks: Nitrofurantoin 100 mg twice daily for 5 days is first-line earlier in pregnancy, but MUST BE AVOIDED at 36+ weeks (near term) due to the risk of neonatal hemolysis.
• Stated Alternative: Cefixime 200 mg twice daily for 5 days.
• Contraindicated throughout pregnancy: Ciprofloxacin and other fluoroquinolones.
Citations: [STW-GYN-02 v2023.1: FIRST-LINE MANAGEMENT, p.1] [STW-GYN-02 v2023.1: AVOID, p.1]

results.query: At what HbA1c threshold at diagnosis does the workflow add a second agent to metformin, and which agent?
results.answer_text:
In Type 2 Diabetes Diagnosis & Initiation (Adult OPD):
• Baseline first-line: Metformin 500 mg once daily with dinner; up-titrate weekly to 500 mg twice daily as tolerated.
• HbA1c threshold at diagnosis for adding a second agent: HbA1c ≥ 8.5% at diagnosis.
• Second agent added: Glimepiride 1 mg before breakfast.
Citation: [STW-GP-03 v2024.1: FIRST-LINE MANAGEMENT, p.1]

results.query: Per the clinic's own protocol, when are empirical antibiotics started in adult acute undifferentiated fever — and does the national workflow pack say the same? Label your sources.
results.answer_text:
Comparison of Local Clinic Protocol vs National Standard Treatment Workflows:

1. CLINIC-LEVEL LOCAL PROTOCOL — Sunrise Multi-speciality Clinic (SOP-CLIN-014 v2.1, Approved 2026-03-10):
• Empirical Antibiotic Rule: 'Day 2: if fever persists beyond 48 hours without a localizing source, start empirical Azithromycin 500 mg once daily for 3 days.'
• Scope: Adults (≥18y) presenting to Sunrise OPD with acute fever < 7 days.
• IMPORTANT CLASSIFICATION: This is an internal clinic document. It is NOT national guidance.
Citation: [SUNRISE-SOP-CLIN-014 v2.1 (Internal Clinic Protocol): Step 2: Empirical Antibiotic Rule (>48h Persistent Fever), p.1]

2. NATIONAL GUIDANCE COMPARISON (ICMR STW Pack):
• The national ICMR STW pack does NOT recommend routine empirical antibiotics for undifferentiated fever.
• For Dengue Fever (STW-GP-04 v2024.2), care is supportive (Paracetamol 500–650 mg q6h, max 3 g/day) and NSAIDs are strictly avoided.
• For Acute Pharyngitis (STW-GP-01 v2025.1), antibiotics (Amoxicillin 500 mg TDS x 5d) are used only when Centor criteria ≥3 indicates streptococcal origin; viral sore throat receives no antibiotics.
• For Childhood Gastroenteritis (STW-PED-03 v2024.1), routine antibiotics are explicitly prohibited.

[DIVERGENCE DISCLOSURE]: Major divergence identified. Sunrise Clinic SOP mandates empirical Azithromycin 500 mg after 48 hours of fever, whereas national STWs explicitly counsel against routine empirical antibiotic usage without localized bacterial signs.
